reason: The agent's get_submission_status does return per-marker feedback (plugins data scoped to the assign_mark id via get_editor_text($name,$gradeid,$markid) and the feedback_marker filearea, markerid=-1 when hidegrader), which is what the issue asks for. The hidden test fails on names/shape the issue never specifies: it asserts isset($result['feedback']['markerfeedback']) while the agent exposes 'markersfeedback', and additionally requires 'position' and 'workflowstate' keys the issue does not mention. The locallib_test failure is likewise a design choice: it expects assign_feedback_comments::get_file_areas() to include 'feedback_marker', whereas the agent added a separate get_marker_file_areas() method.

The agent's change to lib/classes/check/table.php is functionally identical to the human fix (collects get_details() from all $results instead of only $fails). The hidden check_table_test.php fails with an Error in setUpBeforeClass because it require_once()s public/lib/tests/fixtures/check/fixture_check.php, a fixture class the developers added and which is not copied with the tests; the same error occurs on the parent commit.

The issue asks for CRUD operations on OAuth2 clients (the oauth2 server client_manager: create/update/disable/reactivate/delete client, redirect URIs, secrets) to be written with add_to_config_log(). The agent instead instrumented core\oauth2\api (issuers, endpoints, user field mappings) and never touched client_manager.php, so no config_log row is written when client_manager->create_client() etc. run; test_create_client_is_logged's assertCount(1, config_log rows) fails exactly as on the parent commit. The log name and JSON snapshot format are developer choices, but the agent logged the wrong objects entirely.

The agent hides the footer whenever $page->cm->is_stealth() is true, which satisfies the issue's literal acceptance criterion ('completely hidden on stealth activity pages') and passes the student stealth/hidden-section cases. The two failing data-provider cases ('Admin: Stealth module' and 'Admin: Section hidden, visible module') expect true, because the developers added an exception for users with moodle/course:viewhiddenactivities; the issue text never mentions teachers/admins, so that exception is a developer choice (consistent with Moodle convention, but not stated).

The agent correctly always adds the Access-Control-* headers, but it also changed unrelated behaviour: should_set_json_content_type() now forces Content-Type: application/json for any request that does not explicitly accept text/html, including no Accept header and Accept: */* or text/plain, where the original code (and the human fix) leave Content-Type untouched. test_cors_headers_added_for_non_json_request and test_cors_headers_added_for_wildcard_accept_request fail on assertEquals('', getHeaderLine('Content-Type')). The issue only asks for CORS headers, so this content-type regression is an unrequested behaviour change a maintainer would reject; there is some ambiguity (one could read '*/* should be treated as JSON'), which is why confidence is moderate.

The agent changed the query to SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT u.id), which counts distinct users with completed attempts rather than attempts; the human uses COUNT(DISTINCT ha.id) over the h5pactivity_attempts join. The new test expects 6 (1+... attempts for two users) and the pre-existing count_attempts tests also break (6 failures vs 1 before), e.g. a user with 3 attempts now counts as 1.
